title: Deborah
lead: The prophet and judge who called Barak to war against Sisera, Jabin's general, and sang one of the oldest poems in the Bible. Her story and song (Judges 4–5) also give the tent-dweller Jael the final blow.

sections.b:
Deborah is the only judge said to be judging Israel before the crisis comes: people come to her under a palm tree in the hills of Ephraim for decisions (Judges 4:4–5). She is called a prophet, like Miriam before her and Huldah after her (Exodus 15:20; 2 Kings 22:14). She summons Barak with a word from the LORD, goes with him to battle, and says that the honor will go to a woman (Judges 4:6–9). The Song of Deborah (Judges 5) is widely held to be among the oldest Hebrew poems. In Samuel's list of Israel's deliverers the Hebrew has the unknown name Bedan, but the Greek and Syriac read Barak (1 Samuel 12:11), and Hebrews 11:32 names Barak among the people of faith. Psalm 83:9–10 prays for God to treat Israel's enemies "like Sisera, like Jabin at the Kishon River."

The rabbis counted Deborah among the seven women prophets of Israel (Bavli Megillah 14a). Women's leadership in the church and synagogue has often been argued from her story, in both directions.
